title: Haas unveils Godzilla-themed F1 livery before Japanese Grand Prix
content:
TOKYO — Haas has unveiled a special Godzilla-themed livery for its Formula 1 car ahead of this weekend’s Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka.

In an event open to fans in Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, Haas drivers Ollie Bearman and Esteban Ocon helped reveal the new paint scheme which features a silhouette of a fire-breathing Godzilla on both sides of the car.

Further tweaks have been made across the VF-26 car’s traditional red, white and black design, including adjustments to the driver numbers and team name on the sidepods to match the Godzilla branding.

“Godzilla is an icon across the whole world, not only in Japan,” Ocon told The Athletic. “To have him on the car, it’s a big, big thing.”

The idea to find a link between Godzilla and Haas started with a throwaway comment made by the team’s owner, Gene Haas, when discussing ideas for a special livery for last year’s Japanese Grand Prix with Ayao Komatsu, the team principal.

“I was like, ‘OK Gene,’ and kind of didn’t react,” Komatsu told The Athletic. “And then Gene mentioned it three times, and I thought, ‘huh, interesting.’

“Godzilla is someone dynamic, a bit disruptive, and is a Japanese export well-known worldwide. The more I thought about it, the more I thought it was actually a pretty good idea.”

Komatsu still thought it was a long shot, but talks between Haas and Toho, the Japanese company that owns Godzilla’s IP, built up through last year. He then travelled to Tokyo in December to meet Keiji Ota, Toho’s CGO — Chief Godzilla Officer — to finalize plans for the year-long partnership.

Tuesday’s unveiling took place outside Toho’s offices, located on Hibiya Godzilla Square which is overlooked by a statue of Godzilla. Besides this week’s race at Suzuka, Haas and Toho will highlight the partnership around October’s United States Grand Prix ahead of the ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ film release in November.

The partnership marked another major tie-up between Haas and a well-known Japanese brand. In 2024, it entered a technical partnership with Toyota, the racing division of which, TGR, has now become Haas’ title sponsor.

Prior to visiting Tokyo, Ocon, Bearman and Komatsu visited Toyota’s Shimoyama technical center to meet many of the manufacturer’s engineers. They also sampled some of Toyota’s high-end cars on its test track which Ocon described as ‘the craziest track ever.”

The deals have given a greater significance to the Suzuka race week. Bearman said there was “naturally a strong tie” for the team given Komatsu is from Japan.

“Then with strengthening our ties with Toyota as well at the end of last year, and now this Godzilla partnership, it really shows that we are pushing in this Japanese market,” Bearman told The Athletic. “It certainly helps to have a Japanese leader.

As the smallest team on the F1 grid, Komatsu felt Haas could “completely embrace” the Godzilla partnership in a way he thought other, more corporate teams might struggle to do in the same way.

“They’re not disruptive, they’re not dynamic,” Komatsu said. “They’re clean, exclusive, high-end brands. Godzilla isn’t. But most of the things that Godzilla represents, that’s who we are as well. So it’s just like a match made in heaven.”

Haas has done its bit to disrupt F1’s competitive order in the early part of 2026. It currently sits fourth in the constructors’ championship, just one point behind defending champion team McLaren and five points clear of Red Bull.

Bearman has scored all 17 of Haas’ points so far, including a fifth-place finish last time out at the Chinese Grand Prix, only trailing the Mercedes and Ferrari cars. He is fifth in the drivers’ standings, ahead of reigning world champion Lando Norris and four-time champion Max Verstappen.

“It’s been a dream start, honestly,” Bearman said. “The car has been quick, it’s been reliable. It’s been a great start to the year, so I’ve really enjoyed it. I’m so proud of our team. What we’ve been able to do together has been incredible.”
